1.mascotDialogue: Same values, two views — a tree for the ordering rule, an array for how it actually lives in memory. parent(i) equals (i minus 1) over 2. The entire address book.

2.mascotDialogue: Line 3 is the bridge between array and tree — any index's parent is always (i-1)/2, integer division. Line 4 is the min-heap rule itself — stop the moment the parent is already smaller or equal.

3.mascotDialogue: Hover index 4 in the array — watch its tree node light up as a child of index 1. Same data, two synchronised windows onto it.

4.mascotDialogue: Both the array cell and the tree node light in the same broken colour at once — because it is one violation, merely viewed two ways.
